independentReplay.method: Re-rendered PDF page index 54 from the authorized source using get_pixmap(dpi=216, clip=fitz.Rect(boundsPdfPoints), colorspace=csRGB, alpha=False, annots=True); compared RGB sample bytes with the exact pinned candidate PNGs.

harvest.result: The pinned candidate is visually complete and legible, but this independent direct-render replay is not byte/RGB-identical. It differs by at most one channel level at 283 pixels within glyphs; dimensions, crop placement, content, and edges match. Treat the pinned image hash as authoritative and record this renderer-level variance; do not claim exact pixel reproducibility across renderers.

contentFindings.finding: The current wording preserves that when the creature lacks a Strength rating, compare the servant and creature by rolling the appropriate number and type of hit dice, with the higher total stronger. This matches the p.51 continuation. Aerial Servant begins on p.50 and continues on p.51; both source pages were inspected.

The current damage-suffered wording and both examples match the source: sharp cutting weapons work well against fabric, leather, and wood; heavy smashing/crushing weapons work well against wood, stone, and metal. The source leaves object-specific damage capacity to the referee.

The signed direction is correct: subtract one percentage point per level when the cleric is lower; add one point cumulatively when the cleric is higher. The source comparator is the level of the possessor or possessing magic. Current surrounding wording calls this a relative-level adjustment but does not repeat that comparator in the signed sentence; keeping the comparator explicit would make the relation clearer. The source's bare Range 1 and nonreversible title are also preserved.
All six rows match the source. The repeated 7th-level boundary between “up to 7th” and “7th–8th” is retained, as is the source's bare Range 1 with no inferred unit.

The complete four-by-three table matches all twelve printed percentages and asterisk markers. Both footnotes and all four gathering definitions match. “Effectiveness” is an app-added grouping label, not a purported literal source heading; the printed Item, Spell Range, Spell Duration, and Area of Effect labels remain intact, and the source lead-in says the materials reduce spell effectiveness.
